g.title: netviz

ap-ceiling-01 [switch] namespace: hosts Ceiling access point above the machine room, powered over its uplink: 'powered_by: poe' says the run carrying its traffic is its only power path, so it declares no 'power.inputs' at all. The far end of that run is sw-access-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/1, reached across pp-r2-a — a run through a panel is electrically one run for power exactly as it is for frames. labels: env=prod, role=wireless, site=hq vlans: 10 interfaces (4): br0 bridge Vlan10 vlan 10.10.0.4/24 vlan 10 (access) eth0 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 70:69:5a:0c:00:01 wlan0 wifi 70:69:5a:0c:00:10 links (1): eth0 — network/sw-access-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/1 (poe)

g.title: cam-lobby-01 [computer] namespace: hosts Lobby camera, cabled straight to the access switch and powered over that cable. A class-2 PSE port delivers 6.49 W at the powered device, which is what its 5 W draw is checked against (NV-E014). labels: env=prod, role=camera, site=hq vlans: 10 interfaces (1): eth0 ethernet 10.10.0.31/24 vlan 10 (access) ac:cc:8e:0d:00:01 links (1): eth0 — network/sw-access-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/2 (poe)

g.title: rtr-edge-01 [router] namespace: network Edge router for the machine room. It routes between the server VLAN and the outside world, and reaches the core switch over a routed (untagged) copper link in the same rack — the one run in this inventory that does not cross a patch panel. labels: env=prod, role=edge, site=hq interfaces (2): lo0 loopback 192.0.2.1/32 ge-0/0/0 ethernet 10.0.0.1/30 00:05:86:0a:00:00 links (2): psu1 — power/pdu-r1-a:2 (outlet) psu2 — power/pdu-r1-b:2 (outlet)

g.title: sw-access-01 [switch] namespace: network PoE access switch in rack r2. Its uplink leaves the rack through the panel above it, exactly as the server links do; its two PoE ports feed a ceiling access point and a lobby camera, neither of which has a power cord. The switch itself is dual-corded: 'psu1' to the A-side strip, 'psu2' to the B-side one. Both strips are in this rack, and they are on different input feeds, which is what makes 'redundant: true' true (NV-E015). labels: env=prod, role=access, site=hq vlans: 10 interfaces (5): br0 bridge Vlan10 vlan 10.10.0.3/24 vlan 10 (access) GigabitEthernet1/0/1 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:01 GigabitEthernet1/0/2 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:02 GigabitEthernet1/0/24 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:18 links (4): psu1 — power/pdu-r2-a:3 (outlet) psu2 — power/pdu-r2-b:3 (outlet) GigabitEthernet1/0/1 — hosts/ap-ceiling-01:eth0 (poe) GigabitEthernet1/0/2 — hosts/cam-lobby-01:eth0 (poe)

g.title: sw-core-01 [switch] namespace: network Core switch, rack r1. g.title: pdu-r1-a [pdu] namespace: power A-side strip in rack r1, on the utility feed.
